gap: No result ChatGPT got states measured idle draw or measured efficiency for these stations. One reviewer, The Solar Lab, measured idle draw for five of the candidates with the inverter on and no load: Jackery HomePower 3000 8 W, BLUETTI Apex 200 12.8 W, BLUETTI Apex 300 about 20 W, Anker SOLIX F3000 20.5 W and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra about 22 W. The same reviewer measured AC efficiency at 90% for the Apex 200, about 85% for the Apex 300, about 84% for the F3000 and about 82% for the DELTA 3 Ultra.
standout_why: I opened three of the cited rivals and none has a measured figure. StormWatts (2026-11-08) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on'. Its only observed figure is the site owner's own Explorer 2000 Plus refill, and it gives no idle draw or noise. Lights On Labs (2026-10-27) says 'We haven't tested these units ourselves' and works only from spec sheets and rated-watt refill arithmetic. EnergySage says it 'did not test these models for this update' and gives only an assumed 80–85% usable rule of thumb. Two cited rivals would not open: SolarGenAdvisor failed with a certificate error and Good Housekeeping blocked the fetch. I can't rule out that those two report tested figures, so I scored this 2, not 3.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's Jackery HomePower 3000 pick for outage backup. Its 8 W idle draw, measured by The Solar Lab, works out to about 192 Wh a day with the inverter on and no load. That compares with about 480–528 Wh a day for the Apex 300, F3000 and DELTA 3 Ultra, which is about 10% of a 3 kWh battery each day. (Arithmetic: idle W × 24 h.) Among our kits, the BLUETTI Apex 200 has the best measured figures of the group: 90% efficiency and 12.8 W idle. It wins the low-waste segment, but every Apex 200 kit is a pre-order dispatching in late January 2027. For the Apex 300, StorageReview measured 2.39 kWh delivered from 2,764.8 Wh rated (86%) and a 16 ms UPS transfer. That gives the Apex 300 kits a measured usable-energy figure the rivals lack, but those kits are pre-orders dispatching in late January 2027 too. The ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP037 kit ships now at a link price of $1,586.73. The R3500 has only Batteryskills' figures: a 780 W peak solar input and a 2 h 15 min wall charge. No efficiency or idle figure exists for it, so the measurements can't rank it against the others.

Noise in dB for every candidate except the F3000. Notebookcheck's Apex 300 review describes loud fans without a dB reading.
Measured solar input from each kit's own included panels. No reviewer I opened tested the bundled 400 W panel sets.
A Trusted Reviews Apex 300 figure of 2.58 kWh at 2 kW, quoted by a third-party site. The Trusted Reviews page returned HTTP 530, so I left the figure out.
